挿.meaning: Moored by her <part>anchor</part> beside a giant paper <part>sun</part>, a lamplighter pushes a <part>thousand</part> birthday candles into it, one through each tiny hole, until it glows like noon. All night her only job is to <kanji>insert</kanji>.
挿.on: When one won't fit, she rubs it on a bar of <sound>soa</sound>p and it slides right in.
挿.kun: For a joke, she pokes in a <sound>sa</sound>rdine on a stick.

郭.meaning: A ring of walls, with a <part>pennant</part> fluttering on every post, keeps the forest wolves out. Inside, the hens <part>enjoy</part> a picnic, a disco and a hot tub. The wolves peer over the top and sulk: they'd pay to get into that <kanji>enclosure</kanji>.
郭.on: All they get outside is an old fish <sound>carc</sound>ass.
郭.kun: The hens' <sound>coo</sound>k, a <sound>roo</sound>k in an apron, serves them sushi with <sound>wa</sound>sabi.

襟.meaning: A fancy hotel posts a <part>ban</part>: no guests with bare necks. The <part>weathervane</part> from the roof wants the soup of the day, so it spins in the wind until a paper napkin wraps its pole, stiff and starched. The doorman lets it in: nice <kanji>collar</kanji>.
襟.on: At the next table a <sound>kin</sound>gfisher dives straight into its soup.
襟.kun: It dabs the napkin clean with an <sound>e</sound>gg-shaped sponge and a sprig of <sound>ree</sound>d.

蔑.meaning: A <part>sentry</part> guards the palace lawn. A boy runs across the <part>grass</part> swinging a butterfly <part>net</part>, waving, shouting, doing cartwheels. The sentry's eyes never move: his whole job is to <kanji>ignore</kanji> him.
蔑.on: The other guards make <sound>bets</sound> on how long he'll last.
蔑.kun: The boy tries bribes: a <sound>sa</sound>rdine, a pet <sound>ge</sound>cko, a roll of <sound>su</sound>shi. The sentry looks down his nose at all of them.

裸.meaning: A farmer hangs a banana on the <part>weathervane</part> to see which way the wind blows. A cheeky gust peels it in one spin, the skin flying off across three farms. The <part>fruit</part> twirls on top of the barn, totally <kanji>naked</kanji>.
裸.on: The crows on the barn roof flap their wings and cheer, '<sound>Rah</sound>-rah!'
裸.kun: Its peel lands on a <sound>hu</sound>t, bounces off a <sound>du</sound>ck and flops into a <sound>cu</sound>p of tea.

忌.meaning: A <part>cobra</part> curls round a wreath shaped like a <part>heart</part>, wearing a tiny black veil, and sways slowly for its old friend the flute player. For a whole year it won't dance to any tune. Even snakes keep <kanji>mourning</kanji>.
忌.on: It locks the flute in a box and swallows the <sound>key</sound>.
忌.kun: Anyone who tries to play another flute near it gets a hiss and shrieks '<sound>Ee</sound>k!'

蚊.meaning: Every night by your ear, a tiny <part>insect</part> <part>dancer</part> performs her solo, whining one high note as she spins. You clap and clap, but she bows, dodges, and leaves a red itchy bump as her autograph. The star of summer: the <kanji>mosquito</kanji>.
蚊.on: Her biggest fan is a ba<sound>boon</sound>, who scratches his bumps all night.
蚊.kun: You trap her under a <sound>cu</sound>p, but she slips out for an encore.

睡.meaning: A night watchman paints an open <part>eye</part> on each eyelid so his boss thinks he's alert. But his head starts to <part>droop</part>, lower and lower, until the painted eyes stare at his own boots. The boss tiptoes past: he's very <kanji>drowsy</kanji>.
睡.on: Someone tucks a wrapped <sound>swee</sound>t into his top pocket.
睡.kun: He dreams he's waving a butterfly <sound>ne</sound>t, chasing a flying <sound>moo</sound>se.

爽.meaning: A <part>large</part> scarecrow stands in a hot field, arms spread wide, with a wooden <part>lattice</part> strapped under each arm. Every breeze whistles through the gaps, flapping his straw and cooling the crows on his shoulders. Bees queue to sit there: it's so <kanji>refreshing</kanji>.
爽.on: On Sundays the farmer scrubs him with a bar of mint <sound>soa</sound>p.
爽.kun: A crow up there snacks on a <sound>sa</sound>rdine dabbed with <sound>wa</sound>sabi.
